answer.reason: The clause permits ('may') appointing team members from inside or outside the company; the item restates this as optional.
The item keeps the flexibility to set frequency by company needs and the mandatory minimum of at least once a year.
The clause requires ('shall') the frequency to be stated in the procedure, which the item restates exactly.
The item requires a report at the completion of each self-inspection, matching the mandatory clause.
The item lists all three required report contents: results, evaluation and conclusions, and recommended corrective actions.
The item requires an effective follow-up programme, as the clause mandates in the self-inspection context.
The item has management evaluating the self-inspection report and, as necessary, the corrective actions, which matches the mandatory clause.
The clause only suggests ('may be useful') supplementing self-inspections with a quality audit; the item is correctly optional.
The clause says audits 'may' be extended to suppliers and contractors; the item faithfully makes this optional.
The item restates the QC person's shared responsibility, with other relevant departments, for approving reliable suppliers of materials meeting specifications.
The item requires evaluation before approval and inclusion in the approved suppliers' list or specifications, as mandated.
The item includes both required evaluation factors: the supplier's history and the nature of the materials.
The item keeps the condition (if an audit is required) and the purpose of determining the supplier's ability to conform with GMP.
The item restates regular internal audits on an approved schedule to verify GMP compliance for APIs, and is correctly labeled recommended ('should').
The item covers documenting findings and corrective actions and bringing them to responsible management, labeled recommended as per 'should'.
The item requires agreed corrective actions to be completed in a timely and effective manner, labeled recommended as per 'should'.
